stem: A postoperative client is hemodynamically stable and has an order to ambulate as tolerated. Which rationale best explains why the nurse should promote early mobility?

options.A: Early mobility primarily reduces incisional pain and has little effect on pulmonary, vascular, or gastrointestinal recovery
options.B: Early mobility can improve ventilation and secretion clearance, reduce venous stasis, and support return of gastrointestinal function
options.C: Early mobility prevents every postoperative pulmonary and thromboembolic complication, so other prophylactic measures are unnecessary
options.D: Early mobility is used mainly to shorten documentation time and is not a physiologic recovery intervention

rationale: For a stable client who is cleared to ambulate, early mobility supports several systems at once. It promotes ventilation and secretion clearance, reduces venous stasis as part of DVT prevention, and supports gastrointestinal recovery. It complements rather than replaces other prescribed measures such as anticoagulants, compression devices, pulmonary exercises, and adequate pain control.
educational_objective: Explain the multisystem benefits of early postoperative mobility while recognizing that ambulation is individualized and complements other prophylactic interventions.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine / NCBI Bookshelf
source_locator: Table 2.5b Routine Postoperative Nursing Interventions: early ambulation promotes ventilation/removal of secretions and helps prevent atelectasis/pneumonia; early ambulation is among DVT-prevention interventions
source_claim_supported: Early postoperative ambulation, when appropriate, supports pulmonary recovery and is part of thromboembolism prevention; broader NCBI mobility/ERAS sources also support GI recovery.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort — mobility/immobility and assistive care
blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — postoperative mobility
correction_summary: Retained the valid multisystem construct but added hemodynamic stability, an ambulation order, and 'as tolerated' context. Removed any implication that mobility alone prevents all complications or replaces other prophylaxis.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Current NCBI perioperative and mobility content verified.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: Ventilation/secretion clearance, venous-stasis reduction, and GI support are evidence-consistent; no absolute prevention claim retained.
audit_findings.choice_A: Incorrect; mobility has multisystem physiologic effects.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect due to absolute wording and replacement of other prophylaxis.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; mobility is a physiologic recovery intervention.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B accurately states benefits without overclaim.
audit_findings.cueing: Choices are parallel rationales for the same nursing intervention.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Checked fall risk, orthostasis, procedure restrictions, DVT prophylaxis overlap, and overclaim of ileus prevention; stem limits use to a stable client with an order and rationale uses supportive rather than guaranteed language.
